chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the blessings of God upon a man is that his child resembles him.'

key_terms.نِعْمَة: Divine blessing, bounty, or favor bestowed by God
key_terms.يُشْبِهَهُ وَلَدُهُ: That his child resembles him — signifying legitimate lineage and the joy of familial continuity

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about a child resembling their father?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a saying of the Prophet (SAWW) that a child's resemblance to his father is counted among the divine blessings bestowed upon a man. This hadith appears in the chapter on the resemblance of children in the Book of Marriage and Family, reflecting the traditional Islamic view that physical similarity between parent and child is a sign of legitimate parentage and a source of joy. The early Muslim audience understood this as affirming the blessing of clear lineage and the comfort a father finds in seeing his own likeness in his offspring.
